title: Fābulae
summary: Latin stories about the family: a son who won't sleep, a wet dog, the cheese Marcus always forgets, and two daughters who find out they're in the stories. Easy stories or hard ones: which are better? Then Christmas and the Nativity. Quotes: Sinite parvulōs venīre ad mē (Mark 10:14), Glōria in altissimīs Deō (Luke 2:14).

intro.en: Today, let's talk about Latin stories.

lines.en: Hi Marcus. What did you do last night?
lines.la: Salvē, Marce. Quid herī vesperī fēcistī?

lines.en: Last night? First, a battle with my son.
lines.la: Herī vesperī? Prīmum, proelium cum fīliō meō.

lines.en: A battle? Why?
lines.la: Proelium? Cūr?

lines.en: He didn't want to sleep. He wanted to play.
lines.la: Dormīre nōlēbat. Lūdere volēbat.

lines.en: I told a story. Then I sang a Latin song, slowly.
lines.la: Fābulam nārrāvī. Deinde carmen Latīnum lentē cantāvī.

lines.en: And did he sleep?
lines.la: Et dormīvit?

lines.en: Yes. After the third song!
lines.la: Ita. Post tertium carmen!

lines.en: After my son fell asleep, I read Latin stories.
lines.la: Postquam fīlius meus dormīvit, fābulās Latīnās lēgī.

lines.en: Which stories?
lines.la: Quās fābulās?

lines.en: Short stories about my family.
lines.la: Fābulās brevēs dē familiā meā.

lines.en: About your family? Tell me one!
lines.la: Dē familiā tuā? Nārrā mihi ūnam!

lines.en: OK. In the first story, it's raining.
lines.la: Age. In prīmā fābulā pluit.

lines.en: Our dog runs in the rain.
lines.la: Canis noster in pluviā currit.

lines.en: Then he runs into the house, wet!
lines.la: Deinde madidus in domum currit!

lines.en: Madidus? What does it mean?
lines.la: Madidus? Quid significat?

lines.en: That is: full of water, like after a bath.
lines.la: Id est: plēnus aquae, sīcut post balneum.

lines.en: Oh dear! And the children?
lines.la: Ēheu! Et līberī?

lines.en: The dog shakes himself… and the children are wet too!
lines.la: Canis sē quatit… et līberī quoque madidī sunt!

lines.en: A true story. Our dog is always wet.
lines.la: Vēra fābula est. Canis noster semper madidus est.

lines.en: And the second story?
lines.la: Et secunda fābula?

lines.en: In the second, there's no milk at home.
lines.la: In secundā, domī nūllum lac est.

lines.en: So I go to the shop.
lines.la: Ergō ad tabernam eō.

lines.en: I buy milk and bread… but I forget the cheese.
lines.la: Lac et pānem emō… sed cāseum oblīvīscor.

lines.en: The cheese! Did your wife want cheese?
lines.la: Cāseum! Uxor tua cāseum volēbat?

lines.en: Yes. Cheese is very dear to my wife.
lines.la: Ita. Cāseus uxōrī meae valdē cārus est.

lines.en: Dearer than you?
lines.la: Cārior quam tū?

lines.en: Maybe! So I go to the shop again.
lines.la: Fortasse! Ergō iterum ad tabernam eō.

lines.en: With your wife?
lines.la: Cum uxōre tuā?

lines.en: Not with my wife. With my daughters.
lines.la: Nōn cum uxōre meā. Cum fīliābus.

lines.en: My wife stayed at home, with the wet dog.
lines.la: Uxor mea domī mānsit, cum cane madidō.

lines.en: Your stories are true! Are they easy or hard?
lines.la: Fābulae tuae vērae sunt! Facilēsne an difficilēs?

lines.en: Some are easy, some are hard.
lines.la: Aliae facilēs, aliae difficilēs.

lines.en: The easy ones give me help: I learn the words.
lines.la: Facilēs mihi auxilium dant: vocābula discō.

lines.en: The hard ones force me to think in Latin.
lines.la: Difficilēs mē Latīnē cōgitāre cōgunt.

lines.en: If you have to choose: easy or hard?
lines.la: Sī ēligere dēbēs: facilēs an difficilēs?

lines.en: Hmm… the hard ones. But not every day.
lines.la: Hmm… difficilēs. Tamen nōn cotīdiē.

lines.en: I agree with you. For the easy ones make the words firm.
lines.la: Tēcum cōnsentiō. Facilēs enim vocābula firmant.

lines.en: Yesterday, though, something new happened.
lines.la: Herī tamen aliquid novum accidit.

lines.en: My daughters saw the stories.
lines.la: Fīliae meae fābulās vīdērunt.

lines.en: "Dad! We're in the stories!"
lines.la: "Pater! Nōs in fābulīs sumus!"

lines.en: They were very happy. But they decided something at once.
lines.la: Laetissimae erant. Sed statim aliquid cōnstituērunt.

lines.en: What did they decide?
lines.la: Quid cōnstituērunt?

lines.en: They want to choose the next story themselves.
lines.la: Proximam fābulam ipsae ēligere volunt.

lines.en: The older one chose: "The dog eats the cheese."
lines.la: Maior ēlēgit: "Canis cāseum edit."

lines.en: The cheese again!
lines.la: Iterum cāseus!

lines.en: After they chose, my son came in. He wasn't asleep!
lines.la: Postquam ēlēgērunt, fīlius meus intrāvit. Nōn dormiēbat!

lines.en: I wanted to send him back to bed.
lines.la: Eum in lectum remittere volēbam.

lines.en: Let the little children come to me.
lines.la: Sinite parvulōs venīre ad mē.

lines.en: Hmm… who said that?
lines.la: Hmm… quis hoc dīxit?

lines.en: Jesus, in the Gospel of Mark, chapter ten.
lines.la: Iēsus, in Ēvangeliō Marcī, capite decimō.

lines.en: That is: let them come. Don't send them away.
lines.la: Id est: sine eōs venīre. Nōlī eōs dīmittere.

lines.en: Fine. I let the boy stay… but not for long.
lines.la: Bene. Puerum manēre sīvī… sed nōn diū.

lines.en: Christmas is coming. Is there a story about this feast?
lines.la: Nātālis Dominī appropinquat. Estne fābula dē hōc fēstō?

lines.en: There is! The Nativity: Mary, Joseph, the shepherds, the Magi.
lines.la: Est! Nātīvitās: Marīa, Iōsēph, pāstōrēs, magī.

lines.en: An angel is a messenger. He brings the shepherds great news.
lines.la: Angelus nūntius est. Pāstōribus nūntium magnum fert.

lines.en: And the angels sing: Glory to God in the highest.
lines.la: Et angelī cantant: Glōria in altissimīs Deō.

lines.en: Luke wrote that, didn't he?
lines.la: Lūcās hoc scrīpsit, nōnne?

lines.en: Yes, chapter two. And on earth peace to men of good will.
lines.la: Ita, capite secundō. Et in terrā pāx hominibus bonae voluntātis.

lines.en: We sing it at Mass. And after Mass, we have lunch!
lines.la: Hoc in Missā cantāmus. Et post Missam, prandēmus!

lines.en: But your daughters aren't in this story.
lines.la: Sed fīliae tuae in hāc fābulā nōn sunt.

lines.en: No. No dog. No cheese!
lines.la: Minimē. Nūllus canis. Nūllus cāseus!

lines.en: And how do you learn the stories? In one go?
lines.la: Et quōmodo fābulās discis? Ūnō impetū?

lines.en: In one go! ChatGPT always says that.
lines.la: Ūnō impetū! ChatGPT hoc semper dīcit.

lines.en: Yes: three stories without a break.
lines.la: Ita: trēs fābulās sine intermissiōne.

lines.en: I read a line in English and say it in Latin.
lines.la: Versum Anglicē legō et Latīnē dīcō.

lines.en: Then I see it: right, or almost right.
lines.la: Deinde videō: rēctē, aut ferē rēctē.

lines.en: Almost right… like ChatGPT!
lines.la: Ferē rēctē… sīcut ChatGPT!

lines.en: Yes! It always says "almost right."
lines.la: Ita! Semper dīcit: "ferē rēctē."

lines.en: Even when it's right!
lines.la: Etiam sī rēctum est!

lines.en: Bye, Marcus! Say hi to your dear wife and the children.
lines.la: Valē, Marce! Salūtā uxōrem cāram et līberōs.

lines.en: Bye, Iulia! Now I'm going to the shop, to buy cheese.
lines.la: Valē, Iūlia! Nunc ad tabernam eō, ut cāseum emam.
